identity.title: Docket No. 50-482: Licensee Event Report 2022-001-00, “Low Steam

cause.proximate_text: The direct cause of the event was a failure of the valve stem for the 'B' SG MFRV, causing the valve to fail closed and resulting in a loss of feedwater flow control to the 'B' SG. The hardware failure analysis performed on the valve stem determined that the failure of the valve stem was due to stress corrosion cracking (SCC) initiating from the external surface within the region contained within the packing area. The root cause was determined to be that the work instructions for assembling MFRVs were inappropriately updated to include a chemical (anti-seize) that was used in a way that is different than its intended purpose and was introduced into the packing area, causing SCC in the stem until it ultimately failed.
cause.theme: Incorrect maintenance work instructions introduced anti-seize contaminant into valve packing area, causing stress corrosion cracking of stem

nodes.title: Automatic reactor trip due to Low Level in the 'B' SG; MFRV valve stem fracture from fatigue crack propagation

chain: inappropriately updated work instructions introduce anti-seize into packing area [cause TBD] -> (with contributing chrome-plated stem susceptibility) -> stress corrosion cracking of valve stem -> stem fails / MFRV fails closed -> loss of feedwater flow control to 'B' SG -> Low 'B' SG level -> automatic reactor trip, main feedwater isolation, and auxiliary feedwater actuation
notes: Official cause_code/category are TBD/provisional per FORM-366 fields, even though the narrative describes a detailed root-cause and contributing-cause analysis (work-instruction error re: anti-seize use, and chrome-plating susceptibility to SCC); these are captured in proximate_text/theme per rule 4. Two parallel contributing FailureModes (work-instruction anti-seize introduction and chrome-plated stem susceptibility) both feed into the SCC failure mode, per rule 5 parallel-trigger modeling. Previous 2021 event on same valve explicitly stated by licensee to NOT be a repeat event (different failure mechanism - fatigue crack from tool marks vs. SCC), but per rule 9 the reference is still modeled as a stub LER with SIMILAR_TO edge since it is a referenced previous occurrence on the same component. AFW and RPS modeled as involved systems because they were actuated during the event; MFIV mentioned only in system-design context and not separately created as it did not fail or actively participate beyond the automatic main feedwater isolation actuation, which is captured as part of the consequence text rather than as a separate system node to avoid overmodeling design-context references.
